\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{খুব} (khub)}{খুব (khub)}]{\bn{খুব} (khub) — very}

\label{lesson:BN-C370-khub}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for in spite of, then the Bengali for to determine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{খুব}}
\textbf{\bn{খুব}} — \emph{khub} — \textquotedblleft{}very\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{তুমি} \bn{এলে} \bn{আমি} \bn{খুব} \bn{খুশি} \bn{হব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tumi ele āmi khub khushi hôbô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I'll be very happy if you come.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{খুব}} (\emph{khub}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{khūb}, good or fine. In Bengali it became the plain word for 'very'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khub}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khub}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tumi ele āmi khub khushi hôbô.} — I'll be very happy if you come.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for in spite of, then the Bengali for to determine, then say \emph{khub} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{খুব} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Very\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ভীষণ} (bhīshôn)}{ভীষণ (bhīshôn)}]{\bn{ভীষণ} (bhīshôn) — terribly; extremely}

\label{lesson:BN-C370-bhishon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to determine, then the Bengali for very.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ভীষণ}}
\textbf{\bn{ভীষণ}} — \emph{bhīshôn} — \textquotedblleft{}terribly; extremely\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রাস্তায়} \bn{ভীষণ} \bn{ভিড়} \bn{থাকলে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{হেঁটে} \bn{যাব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāstāy bhīshôn bhiṛ thākle āmrā hẽṭe jābô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the streets are terribly crowded, we'll walk.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ভীষণ}} (\emph{bhīshôn}) is Sanskrit \emph{bhīṣaṇa}, terrifying (Monier-Williams). Bengali speech uses it as English uses 'terribly', for anything extreme, good or bad.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhīshôn}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhīshôn}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rāstāy bhīshôn bhiṛ thākle āmrā hẽṭe jābô.} — If the streets are terribly crowded, we'll walk.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to determine, then the Bengali for very, then say \emph{bhīshôn} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{ভীষণ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Terribly; extremely\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বেশি} (beshi)}{বেশি (beshi)}]{\bn{বেশি} (beshi) — more; too much}

\label{lesson:BN-C370-beshi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for very, then the Bengali for extremely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বেশি}}
\textbf{\bn{বেশি}} — \emph{beshi} — \textquotedblleft{}more; too much\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বেশি} \bn{খেলে} \bn{পেট} \bn{ব্যথা} \bn{করবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{beshi khele peṭ bæthā kôrbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you eat too much, you'll get a stomach ache.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বেশি}} (\emph{beshi}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{bēsh}, more. It means 'more' after -\bn{এর} \bn{চেয়ে} and 'too much' on its own.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{beshi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{beshi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{beshi khele peṭ bæthā kôrbe.} — If you eat too much, you'll get a stomach ache.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for very, then the Bengali for extremely, then say \emph{beshi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বেশি} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}More; too much\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কম} (kôm)}{কম (kôm)}]{\bn{কম} (kôm) — less; little}

\label{lesson:BN-C370-kom}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for extremely, then the Bengali for too much.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কম}}
\textbf{\bn{কম}} — \emph{kôm} — \textquotedblleft{}less; little\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দাম} \bn{কম} \bn{হলে} \bn{আমি} \bn{এটা} \bn{কিনব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dām kôm hôle āmi eṭā kinbô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the price is lower, I'll buy this.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কম}} (\emph{kôm}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{kam}, little: the opposite of \bn{বেশি}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kôm}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kôm}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dām kôm hôle āmi eṭā kinbô.} — If the price is lower, I'll buy this.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for extremely, then the Bengali for too much, then say \emph{kôm} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{একটু} (ekṭu)}{একটু (ekṭu)}]{\bn{একটু} (ekṭu) — a little; a bit}

\label{lesson:BN-C370-ektu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for too much, then the Bengali for less.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{একটু}}
\textbf{\bn{একটু}} — \emph{ekṭu} — \textquotedblleft{}a little; a bit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{একটু} \bn{আস্তে} \bn{বললে} \bn{আমি} \bn{বুঝব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ekṭu āste bôlle āmi bujhbô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you speak a bit more slowly, I'll understand.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{একটু}} (\emph{ekṭu}) is \bn{এক}, one (CDIAL 2462 lists Bengali ek), probably with a small-making ending: 'one little bit'. It softens a request: \bn{একটু} \bn{বসো}, do sit down.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ekṭu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ekṭu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ekṭu āste bôlle āmi bujhbô.} — If you speak a bit more slowly, I'll understand.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for too much, then the Bengali for less, then say \emph{ekṭu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{একটু} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A little; a bit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
